mainSignal.title: AI native SDLC is becoming a governed workflow, not a single model.
mainSignal.body: The strongest implementations separate agent reasoning, deterministic execution, independent verification, and privileged approval. QA is increasingly the control layer that makes that autonomy trustworthy.

currentPicture.title: Testing is becoming a control system.
currentPicture.body: Pass rate alone is no longer enough.

currentPicture.title: QA is moving earlier.
currentPicture.body: Specification quality increasingly determines agent quality.

currentPicture.title: Scale comes from decomposition.
currentPicture.body: Large agentic changes become credible when work is split into small, reviewable slices with deterministic acceptance evidence.

currentPicture.title: Permissions are architecture.
currentPicture.body: Reasoning and privileged execution increasingly need separate trust boundaries.

radar.title: Playwright CLI for agents
radar.summary: Browser automation is becoming a native capability for coding and testing agents. Playwright CLI gives agents a compact, deterministic interface for inspection, test generation, execution, diagnosis, and repair without forcing every interaction through a large MCP tool surface.
radar.why: This is a practical bridge between coding agents and mature browser automation. It also reinforces a broader pattern: use deterministic tools underneath the agent and reserve model reasoning for interpretation and decision making.

radar.title: Policy separated CI agents
radar.summary: The strongest agentic CI pattern separates read and reasoning privileges from write and execution privileges. Agents investigate, propose, and explain while a controlled deterministic layer validates and performs privileged actions.
radar.why: This reduces the blast radius of autonomous tooling and gives enterprises a clearer audit boundary. It is increasingly relevant to CI modernization, security review, and AI readiness assessments.

radar.title: Independent agent quality gates
radar.summary: A green test run is no longer enough evidence for agent generated work. Newer approaches add independent graders, review constraint checks, trajectory review, mutation style validation, and other forms of second order verification.
radar.why: The same agent that wrote code or tests can share the same blind spots. Independent evaluation creates a more credible acceptance layer and is becoming one of the most important QA architecture questions for AI driven teams.

radar.title: Spec to test enrichment
radar.summary: QA reasoning is moving earlier in the lifecycle. Agents and test architects can expose ambiguity, derive acceptance constraints, and turn business intent into more machine verifiable specifications before implementation starts.
radar.why: Agent quality is bounded by input quality. Teams with vague requirements and undocumented rules will get less reliable autonomous development than teams that deliberately improve specification quality.
references: Agentic SDLC with a QA engineering mindset

radar.title: Adversarial test validation
radar.summary: Generated tests can pass while still being weak. Mutation testing, adversarial examples, alternate implementations, and independent test generation are emerging as ways to verify that a suite can distinguish correct behavior from plausible mistakes.
radar.why: This addresses a core AI testing bias: code and tests can agree with each other while both are wrong. Strong validation asks whether the tests would fail against believable incorrect implementations.

radar.title: MCP as a QA surface
radar.summary: MCP servers are becoming APIs for agents. As adoption grows, they need the same engineering discipline applied to other integration surfaces: contracts, compatibility checks, access control, observability, and regression testing.
radar.why: A broken or over privileged MCP tool can make an otherwise capable agent unreliable or unsafe. This creates a new testing and governance surface that many teams have not yet incorporated into their QA strategy.

radar.title: Multi agent coding workflows
radar.summary: Multiple coding agents can provide useful drafting, critique, specialization, and escalation, but simply adding more agents does not reliably improve outcomes. Coordination, isolation, and explicit acceptance rules matter more than agent count.
radar.why: This is promising for complex work, but architecture and orchestration are still evolving quickly. It is better treated as a controlled experiment than a default delivery model today.

agentic.title: Agentic SDLC
agentic.summary: The durable pattern is a governed workflow: agents handle interpretation and planning, deterministic systems handle reproducible execution, and policy boundaries control privileged actions.
points: Use agents where reasoning is valuable, not as a replacement for every deterministic step.
Separate read and reasoning privileges from write and deployment privileges.
Favor focused workflows that can be observed and evaluated over broad autonomy claims.

qa.title: QA and testing
qa.summary: QA is moving from downstream verification toward specification quality, evidence design, independent validation, and control of autonomous workflows.
points: Generated tests need quality gates beyond pass rate and coverage.
Specification enrichment is becoming a meaningful pre implementation QA activity.
Narrow autonomous agents for consistency, test gaps, and failure investigation look more practical than broad autonomous QA.

evaluation.title: Evaluation and governance
evaluation.summary: The central problem is trust. Teams need objective evidence that agent generated work is correct, acceptable, auditable, and produced within bounded authority.
points: Evaluate trajectories and constraints, not only final pass or fail outcomes.
Keep independent verification separate from the implementation context where practical.
Treat permissions, runtime isolation, and human acceptance authority as architecture.

mcp.title: MCP and tooling
mcp.summary: MCP is becoming a real integration layer for agent workflows, which also makes it a first class QA, security, and observability surface.
points: Test MCP servers independently from the model that consumes them.
Use MCP when richer persistent interaction is valuable, not simply because it is available.
Treat tool contracts, access scopes, and traces as part of the quality architecture.

coding.title: Coding agents
coding.summary: Coding agents can now contribute to production modernization at very large scale, but the successful pattern is decomposition, strong deterministic feedback, incremental rollout, and human control rather than unconstrained autonomy.
points: Break large migrations and refactors into independently reviewable slices.
Use tests, compilers, linters, and static analysis as fast acceptance feedback for agent work.
Keep human judgment focused on architecture, quality gates, exceptions, and whether the work is actually complete.

consulting.title: Top consulting questions
consulting.summary: These questions increasingly distinguish a basic AI adoption review from a useful agentic SDLC assessment.
points: Are requirements explicit enough for agents to act on safely?
Can generated code and generated tests be independently validated?
Does CI expose enough evidence for agent investigation and diagnosis?
Are agent permissions separated from privileged execution?
Can large migrations or refactors be decomposed into small, independently verifiable slices?
Can the team measure agent quality beyond a green pipeline?
Are autonomy thresholds, run limits, and human escalation paths explicit?
Can the organization reconstruct why an agent made a change from traces and artifacts?
